messages.text: We did the two-day coastal ride at the weekend. Marek from work and his daughter Zofia came with me, and Zofia had a puncture before we were even a mile out of the car park.
A puncture inside the first mile. I hope she saw the funny side of it.
She did. On the second day it rained so hard that we gave up at the ferry slip and got a lift back in a farmer's van with the bikes in the trailer.
Giving up at the ferry slip in that rain sounds like sense rather than defeat.
The garage wants a yes or no on the clutch repair by Friday and I keep not ringing them back.
A Friday deadline that you keep stepping around. It sounds like the answer is not easy yet.
What did I tell you about the bike ride?
Sorry, I cut that short. Just remind me who rode with me.

You rode with Marek from work and his daughter Zofia — she's the one who got the puncture before you'd gone a mile out of the car park. The two-day coastal ride, at the weekend. And no need to apologise for cutting it short.
And how did the second day turn out?
Leave the ride. It is the clutch business that is actually nagging at me today.

Fair enough — the ride's parked.

So it's the clutch. A yes or no by Friday, and the phone keeps staying in your pocket. I don't think the not-ringing is laziness. Something about the answer itself is stuck, whether that's the cost or just committing to it.
I think I will just ring them and say go ahead.

Then you've said it out loud, and that's usually the bit that was stuck. Go ahead is a yes — nothing left to weigh up, just a phone call.

I hope it's a relief once it's done.
